summary: Storage platform work for application teams across the firm, from provisioning and backups to reconciliation and the move to a lakehouse.

highlights.text: Led the migration of the team's sensitive, write-heavy data stores from the data lake to the lakehouse, coordinating the cutover with the teams that build dashboards and reports on them.
Engineered Kafka-based change data capture for the team's long-running reconciliation jobs, replacing scheduled batch extracts with change streams so downstream teams see data as it lands.
Migrated 90+ TB of long-term records from on-premises storage to AWS S3 archival, reclaiming the capacity previously provisioned to hold them.
Developed the team's Python services behind the REST and GraphQL APIs for storage provisioning and management, replacing manual requests with automation.

Built and extended the backup management software in Java and Spring Boot, adding reconciliation jobs that check backups against the source and reworking legacy backup paths application teams depend on.
Handled production incidents on the team's on-call rotation, from stuck reconciliation jobs to stale data, and turned each root cause into an alert or runbook so the next one was caught sooner.
Designed Grafana dashboards and alerts behind the team's reconciliation and backup runs, covering API health, job status, and capacity metrics for the storage products.
Owned the scheduling layer behind the team's reconciliation runs, covering Autosys job definitions and their triggers.
Mentored new hires and junior engineers, walking them through the systems and reviewing their code changes.

summary: Built faculty scheduling and student field-tracking applications, plus the integrations and deployment pipeline behind them.

highlights.text: Built a Java/Spring Boot, Hibernate, React, and PostgreSQL scheduling application for faculty, reducing administrative workload by ~40%.
Shipped the Student Field Tracker in Angular, TypeScript, C#, ASP.NET, and SQL Server, with ~60% faster retrieval.
Integrated Zoom APIs with OAuth 2.0 and C++ web scraping to analyze meeting engagement, then built the visualizations on top of it.
Automated deployment of the application and its database through AWS DevOps pipelines.

summary: Built real-time streaming and the client-facing interface on top of it, including the encrypted transport for client data.

highlights.text: Deployed Apache Kafka for real-time streaming, so downstream services consumed data as it was produced instead of waiting on scheduled batch runs.
Built the client-facing React app and its Redux store on a Flask API, plus the SSL/TLS transport layer in C++, with zero reported breaches over six months.
Cleaned and reshaped client data in Python before it moved downstream.
Hosted the application on AWS EC2 with its database on RDS.

summary: Built domestic and overseas payment flows in Java Spring Boot microservices, with the testing and release automation around them.

highlights.text: Built domestic and overseas client payment flows in Java Spring Boot microservices and Spring MVC.
Tested transaction workflows with JUnit and Mockito before release, catching defects in review, not production.
Automated the release path with Jenkins and Kubernetes, cutting deployment errors across releases.
